name: Multilingual Cultural-Grounded Evaluation with Contextual Anchors
description: This paper introduces a culturally grounded, multilingual benchmark for evaluating the performance of large language models (LLMs) across more than 30 languages and dialects. Moving beyond existing metrics that emphasize factual correctness or translation fidelity, the benchmark integrates cultural context anchors. These anchors are semantically rich constructs derived from regional folklore, customary law, traditional medicine, idiomatic usage, and spiritual systems. Using a structured rubric developed in collaboration with domain experts, the benchmark assesses semantic appropriateness, cultural resonance, contextual fidelity, and representational sensitivity. Evaluations conducted on leading LLMs including GPT-4, Claude, and LLaMA reveal significant inconsistencies in culturally anchored responses, particularly in low-resource languages. The benchmark is extensible, integrates seamlessly with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) pipelines, and aims to establish a new standard for evaluating cultural fidelity in generative AI.
evaluation_method: human evaluation of cultural grounding and contextual appropriateness (human-rated relevance/appropriateness scores), potentially supplemented by automatic semantic-similarity checks
reputation: New academic benchmark proposed for evaluating cultural grounding across languages; early-stage adoption primarily within research groups focused on multilingual and cultural evaluation.
notes: Subjective human judgments drive primary evaluation — susceptible to annotator bias and cultural perspective effects. Multilingual coverage and annotator composition critically affect results; not an LLM-contamination risk in the usual sense but sensitive to cultural/contextual annotation quality.
